newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Restructuring boosts Gamma first-half net.
newsitem.headline: Restructuring boosts Gamma first-half net.

text.p: Dutch textiles group Gamma said on Tuesday first-half profits had been buoyed by restructuring at two of its subsidiaries and a shift in its product mix.
The company reported first-half net earnings up 22 percent at 24.7 million guilders from a year-earlier 20.23 million.
"This improvement was due both to restructuring measures at Vlisco and Texoprint which were fully reflected in 1996 and a change in the sales mix," Gamma said in a statement.
Lower raw material prices and generally favourable exchange rates had also boosted the bottom line, it added.
It said the upturn in sales of printed textiles on the African market which began in 1995 had continued into 1996.
However its interior decoration business was still struggling in the face of lower spending on consumer durables, it said.
Technical textiles performed worse year-on-year, but had staged a partial recovery compared to the second half of 1995, it said.
For the full year, the textiles maker is forecasting net profit some 20 percent higher than last year's 41.46 million guilders.
